newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan says November inflation falls to 133 pct.
newsitem.headline: Sudan says November inflation falls to 133 pct.

text.p: Sudanese inflation dropped to 133 percent in November from 166 percent in July, Finance Minister Abdel Wahab Osman said in comments published on Monday.

The government-owned daily newspaper al-Ingaz al-Watani quoted Osman as saying the reduction was a result of measures such as controlling money supply, stabilising the exchange rate and reducing government spending.
Osman told parliament last week that under the 1997 budget inflation would fall to 70 percent from 160 percent.

Inflation is a major problem for Sudan and the government has made fighting it a top priority. It has imposed a tight monetary regime on almost every department and many in the private sector have complained of a lack of liquidity.

The government has also reduced its demand for hard currency and has launched extensive campaigns to catch those dealing illegally in hard currency, in an attempt to reduce or stabilise the rate of the pound to the dollar.
Since July 120 people have been sentenced to between three months and five years for dealing illegally in foreign currency.

The exchange rate has registered little change over the past few months. The official rate for the dollar has remained 1,454 Sudanese pounds since August while the dollar buys about 1,700 pounds on the black market, down from about 2,000 in July.
